Core Motion Rules: The Topic Gibbon's default entrance begins with a brief environmental cue before the character is fully visible. Foliage or a branch moves first, then the gibbon emerges from the canopy edge in a controlled downward swing/drop. The descent stays compact with flexed legs; in a direct-release variant the legs extend shortly before touchdown, while a branch-assisted variant may keep one hand attached until the feet reach the ground. Landing is feet-first and absorbed through deep hip/knee flexion. A brief hand/knuckle stabilization can occur but is not required; REF-ARRIVAL-003 shows a clean no-hand-brace profile landing. Crucially, the landing never becomes a held pose: the body rebounds directly into the first bipedal strides and the arms remain high/outward for balance. The result is one continuous canopy-to-ground arrival ending in a readable walk toward or across the user view.
Must Preserve: Environmental anticipation or branch motion; hidden-to-visible emergence; flexed/tucked descent; terminal leg preparation for ground contact; feet-first landing; deep lower-body impact absorption; optional rather than mandatory hand support; no static pause after landing; immediate transition into recognizable gibbon ground gait; arms remain available for balance
Can Vary: Swing vs drop proportion; exact support hand; amount of branch bow/recoil; lead side; landing height; whether the hand stays attached until foot contact; whether a ground brace occurs; exact foot ordering; frontal vs side arrival angle; speed of first steps
Avoid: Sudden appearance with no anticipation; teleport-like drop; superhero landing held as a pose; long flashy brachiation before orientation; hard cut from landing to walking; mandatory ground hand brace; exaggerated branch physics; locked-knee landing; forcing identical arrival geometry every time
V1 Simplification: V1 hybrid entrance: 0.5–1.5s authored canopy rustle / branch movement → brief visible descent, optionally with one-arm branch support → feet-first landing + deep flexion → optional stabilizing hand touch → immediate frontal/front-three-quarter/side walk-in → existing Stop / Sit / Settle. In a direct-release variant, tuck through descent and extend the legs only near touchdown. Keep any branch bow/recoil restrained and authored.
Open Questions: No critical V1 gap remains. Side-view evidence confirms the landing can resolve entirely through the lower body without a hand brace.

Core Motion Rules: Across speeds and viewing angles, ground locomotion is bipedal with persistently flexed hips and knees, mild-to-moderate forward torso pitch, pronounced lateral trunk sway, rhythmic pelvic elevation/drop and rotation, loose wrists/hands, and a comparatively stable head. Arm carriage is variable and balance/context-dependent rather than a strict speed rule. Rear and rear-three-quarter references confirm pelvic list/rotation, lateral body shift, wide-to-semi-tandem foot placement and mild toe-out.

Avoid: Straight-kneed human gait; symmetrical human-style arm pumping; rigid wrists; minimal lateral sway; one fixed arm pose at all speeds; head bobbing in lockstep with torso; eliminating pelvic roll from rear view; hard-coding arm height to speed
V1 Simplification: For V1, build at least two pace states: calm walk with continuous ground support and smoother cadence, and faster ground locomotion with quicker cadence / stronger forward pitch. In both, preserve bent joints, lateral roll, pelvic oscillation, loose hands and stable head. Let arm height vary between low/outward and elevated-abducted based on pose balance and authored variation rather than speed alone.
Open Questions: Closed for V1. The gait is sufficiently corroborated across pace and viewing angle.

Core Motion Rules: The Topic Gibbon visibly decelerates before sitting: final strides shorten, forward travel reduces, and the centre of mass drops mostly vertically through deep ankle, knee and hip flexion. The pelvis settles into a low, wide seated / semi-crouched base. Arms transition from locomotion balance into descent balance and then directly toward the next interaction. Ground support is optional: the stair reference uses a brief hand brace, while two flat-ground references complete the descent entirely through the lower body with both hands free. Small pelvic/haunch/foot adjustments complete the settle. The head stays comparatively steady toward the interaction target. A short stable beat marks entry into the ready/input state.

Can Vary: Hand bracing may occur or not; exact final foot/leg asymmetry; degree of torso pitch; descent speed; exact seated contact depth
Avoid: Instant run-to-sit snap; human chair-sit mechanics; both arms frozen overhead after stopping; mandatory hand brace; freezing immediately on contact; exaggerated collapse; unnecessary pause before reaching
V1 Simplification: Use a compact four-beat transition: brake → drop → settle → ready/reach. Default flat-ground sit is lower-body driven with hands free so the arms can transition directly into receiving context/food. Use a brief support-hand touch only when slope, speed or instability makes it useful.
Open Questions: No critical gap remains for V1. Additional references are V2 refinement only.

Core Motion Rules: The Topic Gibbon receives an offering with one long-arm reach from a controlled low crouched / seated state. Full static settling is not required: the reach may begin while the pelvis is still completing its descent, or it may start from a fully seated base. The reaching shoulder moves forward and the elbow extends along a low, direct path; the wrist stays relaxed and slightly pronated. Long fingers pre-curve, then sweep/curl inward in a hook-wrap to secure the object into the palm/base rather than using a fine human precision pinch. Once secure, the elbow flexes quickly and retracts the object inward, usually toward the mouth, with minimal extra torso motion. Repeated grabs reset by lowering the reaching arm back toward the offering before repeating the same loop. The opposite hand may brace or remain free depending on stability needs.
Must Preserve: One-arm reach; low direct approach; relaxed slightly pronated wrist; long-finger hook-wrap grip; clear object security before retraction; quick elbow-flexion retraction; controlled low body state; minimal torso disturbance; reusable reset between repeated grabs
Can Vary: Reach may begin after full settle or during final lowering; which hand reaches; whether opposite hand braces; exact torso lean; thumb contribution; retraction target; whether repeated grabs include a full hand reset
Avoid: Human-style thumb-index precision pinch; dainty fingertip pickup; large torso lunge; symmetrical two-hand grab; stiff wrist; requiring a full static sit before every grab; mandatory support-hand contact; overcomplicated hand choreography between repeated grabs
V1 Simplification: Use a four-beat receive loop: orient → extend → hook-wrap → retract. For repeated inputs, add a simple reset by lowering the reaching hand back toward the offering and replaying the same loop. Default calm flow can start after the ready beat; a faster variant may overlap reach/grab with the final settle. Opposite-hand bracing is optional.
Open Questions: No critical Receive Food / Receive Context gap remains for V1. Fine thumb/finger geometry can be refined later with clearer close-ups.

Core Motion Rules: The Topic Gibbon processes food from a stable seated base using modular, interruptible sub-actions. It may secure one or multiple items. For larger or multiple fruits, one hand can retain a reserve while the other feeds/manipulates. For a small morsel, one active hand can repeatedly inspect, lift, bite/shear, lower and reorient the item between bites. The hand-to-mouth path is short and direct; the head may dip slightly to meet it. Chewing is rhythmic, while gaze quickly decouples from the food to scan left/right/up. Food may be rotated or digit-rolled before another bite. Unwanted pits/skins/remnants can be casually dropped/spat or cleared manually, but discard is optional when the item is consumed directly. Small independent upper-limb actions can coexist with chewing. At natural breakpoints, the loop can reset to another bite/item or hand off into waiting, result-ready, or locomotion.
Must Preserve: Stable seated base; direct hand-to-mouth bite/shear; rhythmic chewing; head/gaze scanning independent of chewing; in-hand manipulation/reorientation when needed; casual discard when remnants exist; natural reset/handoff; modular interruptible structure
Can Vary: One vs multiple items; active/reserve hand assignment; number/size of bites; exact scanning pattern; hand transfer; food rotation amount; oral vs manual discard; whether discard occurs at all; small secondary arm actions
Avoid: Frozen chewing with no head movement; human-style neat eating; identical repeated loops; mandatory pit discard in every cycle; exaggerated throwing when references show casual drop/spit; forcing the full sequence to finish before AI result; making one hand biologically dominant
V1 Simplification: Build Family 4 as interruptible modules. Large-fruit mode: bite → chew/scan → optional manipulate → optional discard → next item/reset. Small-morsel mode: inspect → lift → bite/shear → lower → chew/scan → digit-roll/reorient → repeat. Exit at the next natural breakpoint when AI finishes; otherwise chain modules or transition into Family 5 Processing / Waiting.
Open Questions: No critical gap remains for V1. Additional food types, discard close-ups, or alternate angles are V2 refinement.

Canonical Motion Spec: Processing / Waiting - Quiet Sit / Look Around
Core Motion Rules: The Topic Gibbon can wait in a compact, self-contained seated posture with almost no root translation. Hips and knees remain deeply flexed, the spine is relaxed and rounded forward, and the long arms either gather around the tucked legs or drape passively along the lap/knees/substrate. Torso motion is limited to faint breathing. The head and gaze are the main baseline active channels: slow deliberate turns or small ambient scans occur between multi-second still holds without dragging the shoulders, torso or pelvis into the movement. During longer waits, an occasional localized self-scratch may be layered onto this base: one hand lifts to the head/cheek/upper neck, performs rapid small-amplitude scratches with only slight neck/upper-torso accommodation, then lowers back to rest without changing the seated footprint.
Must Preserve: Compact folded seated base; deeply flexed legs; rounded relaxed spine; stable contact footprint; near-zero root/pelvis translation; subtle breathing; sparse head/gaze movement with long holds; passive/gathered long arms; clean return to baseline after any optional scratch
Can Vary: Exact hand and knee arrangement; arms wrapped vs draped; head-turn direction and hold duration; amount of chin tilt; whether optional scratch occurs; scratching hand and exact head/neck target
Avoid: Continuous fidgeting; constant head scanning; large torso rotations following head turns; loose arms drifting for no reason; obvious short mechanical loop; exaggerated breathing; repetitive scratching as the baseline idle; scratching that shifts the whole body or seated footprint
V1 Simplification: Use the quiet sit as the lowest-energy Processing / Waiting state: mostly still base + faint breathing + occasional head/gaze turn with long holds. For longer latency, optionally insert one short scratch module: hand lifts → rapid local scratch → hand lowers → exact idle recovery. Keep it interruption-safe and hand off at natural still points to result-ready or another processing behavior.
Open Questions: No critical gap remains for V1. Perched idle, grooming, and additional low-energy behaviors can be researched as separate variants.
Next Reference Needed: None required for V1 quiet sit

Core Motion Rules: The Topic Gibbon announces a completed result from a stable seated base with pelvis, feet and support contacts planted. The lower body and lumbar/root region remain passive while the expressive motion is concentrated in the thorax, neck, jaw/lips and head. At the call apex, the head and neck extend strongly upward/back, the chest lifts/expands, and the mouth opens into an extreme vertically elongated rounded/funnel-like gape. Long arms hang or brace low as relaxed stabilizing struts rather than gesturing. Repeated vocal pulses produce small thoracic/cervical contractions and rapid mouth cycling between full and partial funnel shapes without translating the root. As intensity decays, the mouth narrows/closes, the chest relaxes, and the head may drop/turn asymmetrically before the spine settles back into a rounded seated rest.
Must Preserve: Stable seated/root footprint; passive pelvis/lumbar base; low relaxed arm/hand stabilizers; strong upward head/neck extension; unmistakable extreme funnel-like call mouth; chest/throat expansion and pulse; rapid wide-to-partial mouth cycling during staccato calls; clear seated recovery that can include a quick asymmetric head drop/turn; mute-readable silhouette
Can Vary: Exact preparatory mouth shape; exact head pitch; number/speed of pulse beats; symmetric vs asymmetric leg placement; one-hand vs two-hand bracing; degree of lip flare; whether recovery head turn is left/right; optional sound level
Avoid: Whole-body jumping; arm flailing; pelvic/root rocking; visible foot repositioning; tiny mouth movement that cannot read muted; cartoon scream disconnected from thorax/neck mechanics; mechanical identical pulse looping; forced audio; slow symmetrical fade when an abrupt natural recovery is more appropriate
V1 Simplification: Use a short rooted result-ready sequence: small preparation/compression → head/chest lift → extreme wide-mouth apex → one or two smaller thorax/mouth pulse beats → quick re-level or asymmetric head drop/turn → relaxed seated settle. Keep pelvis/feet/support contacts planted. Sound is optional; the visual must carry completion when muted. Natural left/right asymmetry in legs and bracing is acceptable.
Open Questions: Closed for V1. No critical motion gap remains.

Canonical Motion Spec: Processing / Waiting - Active Transition: Sit → Rise → Run → Catch → First Swing
Core Motion Rules: The Topic Gibbon moves from quiet seated processing into active arboreal motion as one continuous chain with overlapping transitions and no neutral pose resets. From sitting, the torso pitches forward and the pelvis rises through hip/knee extension while forward translation begins before full standing; supporting hands release early and long arms sweep directly into lateral balancing carriage as the first stride begins. The gait develops into the known bent-knee, laterally swaying ground locomotion. Near the canopy, the body performs a visible COM preload / crouching dip, redirects forward velocity into an upward-forward launch, and reaches for the branch before contact. The first catch occurs while airborne near the apex / early descent. Load transfers immediately into the shoulder, the legs tuck for clearance, and forward velocity continues directly through the first pendulum bottom into the beginning of the backswing / next-arm engagement without a static hang.
Must Preserve: No static stand between sitting and locomotion; forward translation begins during pelvic ascent; arms transition directly from support/rest into balancing carriage; first stride overlaps the rise; visible COM preload before takeoff; overhead reach begins before branch contact; catch occurs while airborne; immediate tensile shoulder loading; leg tuck/clearance; uninterrupted momentum through first pendulum and into the next swing beat
Can Vary: Initial support hand; first stepping foot; exact rise timing; lead arm/side; exact takeoff foot pattern; preload depth; torso pitch; amount of leg tuck; branch angle/height; degree of arm asymmetry; exact timing of secondary-arm engagement
Avoid: Sit → full neutral stand → walk; arms dropping into a neutral hang between states; snapping from seated pose to gait; stopping at the branch before swinging; snapping from run to hanging pose; rigid shoulder at catch; straight dangling legs into obstacles; any velocity reset at grip contact; over-specifying a one-foot or two-foot launch when the footage does not resolve it
V1 Simplification: V1 chain: quiet sit → forward pitch + pelvic rise → arms peel off support into lateral balance → first stride before full upright → accelerate into ground gait → visible preload → upward-forward launch + overhead target → airborne catch near apex → immediate shoulder stretch + leg tuck → first pendulum bottom → begin backswing / next-arm engagement. Treat every boundary as an overlap, never a hard state cut.
Open Questions: No critical V1 motion gap remains, but keep 5B open for refinement while rare bridge footage is still being collected. Exact takeoff-foot timing and fine finger closure remain the main unresolved micro-details.
Next Reference Needed: Optional: clearer side takeoff-foot / hand-contact view or end-to-end sit/eat→run→catch→swing clip

Canonical Motion Spec: Swing / Brachiation - Core Loop + Hang + Direction Change + Exit
References Used: REF-SWING-001; REF-SWING-002; REF-SWING-003; REF-SWING-004; REF-SWING-005; REF-SWING-006; cross-reference REF-ARRIVAL-003 for direct ground exit
Core Motion Rules: Steady-state brachiation is a continuous alternating single-arm pendulum. One arm supports and elongates under load as the body passes through the downswing; the free arm reaches to the next hold; near upswing the new hand catches and the previous hand releases with little prolonged two-hand dwell. Legs remain flexed overall with modest extension/tuck modulation and the torso rotates toward the reach. The path need not remain linear: at canopy corners or orthogonal supports, the pivot arm can take load while the torso yaws and the free arm redirects toward a new beam, preserving momentum through 90° or 180° turns. In natural canopies, longer drop arcs and variable branch geometry create larger-amplitude swings. Rare energetic play can include looping/pivoting around one support or rebound transfers using compliant branches, but these are optional flourishes rather than baseline mechanics. Longer processing may decay into a quiet hang and restart through core/leg tuck plus shoulder engagement. Exits can resolve into perch, platform/ground landing, or direct steep descent.
Must Preserve: Alternating single-arm support; smooth relay; tensile shoulder loading; continuous pendulum momentum; subtle torso rotation toward reach; flexed legs with extension/tuck modulation; free-arm targeting before transfer; no pose reset at catches or direction changes; directional changes achieved through pivot load + torso yaw + redirected reach; physically continuous hang entry/re-entry and exits
Can Vary: Which arm starts; exact cycle timing; branch spacing; swing amplitude; degree of torso yaw; whether the route is straight, diagonal, 90° or 180°; whether a hanging pause occurs; whether rare one-branch looping/rebound play occurs; exit type
Avoid: Static hang between every swing; long two-hand pauses in steady-state motion; rigid symmetrical torso; stiff straight legs; velocity reset at catches or corners; teleporting between non-aligned supports; making acrobatic loops mandatory; requiring fully simulated elastic branch physics; landing with locked knees
V1 Simplification: V1 baseline: repeatable alternating swing loop with modest torso yaw and leg modulation. Optional variations: corner turn via pivot-arm load + yaw + next hold; long-amplitude natural-canopy arc; calm hang/re-entry; rare energetic one-branch loop or rebound transfer. Keep all variations interruptible. Use authored branch bend/recoil only when needed. Exit to perch, supported platform landing, or direct feet-first ground descent.
Open Questions: No critical V1 gap remains. Additional references are refinement only. Do not expand complexity unless a clip reveals a genuinely new product-useful behavior.
Next Reference Needed: Optional only: exceptionally clear grip-release close-up, rear/diagonal natural-canopy route, or second vertical-ascent reference

Canonical Motion Spec: Processing / Waiting - Vertical Arboreal Ascent / Tree-to-Tree Climb
Core Motion Rules: Vertical arboreal ascent is distinct from horizontal brachiation. The Topic Gibbon uses vertical or oblique trunks as temporary supports and launch surfaces, combining high arm contacts with active foot pushes to redirect momentum upward. REF-ASCENT-001 shows repeated upward transfers between supports; REF-ASCENT-002 confirms the same mechanics from another angle in a shorter trunk-scramble → upward/lateral spring → high branch catch sequence. The body alternates between extension during reach/suspension and compact hip/knee tuck during transfer. Each catch continues the ascent rather than settling into a level pendulum, and a final high catch can flow immediately into suspended swing/hang.
Must Preserve: Clear elevation gain; active foot use against vertical substrate; high arm catches; extension-to-tuck body modulation; continuous upward momentum redirection; no neutral pause before launch/catch; torso orientation changing toward the next higher support; immediate shoulder loading after high catch
Can Vary: Which hand leads; exact foot-contact pattern; one- vs two-foot final thrust; amount of trunk/branch bend; degree of airborne flight vs short suspended swing; torso twist; branch spacing; number of upward transfers before settling
Avoid: Treating ascent as flat horizontal brachiation; passive dangling legs throughout; teleporting upward; full stop before every higher catch; locking exact foot sequence from blurred footage; requiring complex branch physics; snapping from climb directly to hanging pose
V1 Simplification: V1 ascent module: trunk high-grip / foot-supported climb → compact preload → foot-driven upward/oblique spring → high overhead catch → immediate shoulder loading + leg tuck → suspended swing/hang. For a longer restless sequence, chain one or two additional higher catches using REF-ASCENT-001-style transfers. Use restrained authored branch bend only if visible.
Open Questions: No critical V1 gap remains. A second multi-transfer ascent or clearer foot-push close-up would improve fidelity but is not required.
Next Reference Needed: Optional: another multi-transfer vertical ascent or clearer launch/catch close-up

Canonical Motion Spec: Departure / Exit - Ground Interaction → Canopy Departure
Core Motion Rules: The Topic Gibbon leaves a ground interaction as one continuous state change rather than fading out or resetting to neutral. The invariant is orientation away from the interaction followed immediately by committed locomotion into the canopy. Two supported routes are valid. Route A: from seated/resting/feeding, attention and center of mass shift forward, the rise overlaps the first stride, arms move directly into balance, 2–3 brisk steps accelerate into an upward-forward leap, the canopy is targeted before/during takeoff, the catch occurs while airborne, and momentum becomes the first suspended swing/pull-up. Route B: from the same low interaction state, the gibbon pivots roughly 180° away, launches directly to a nearby vertical trunk, establishes hand/foot contact, climbs continuously for a few beats, and resolves into a high perch or disappearance. Both routes avoid a neutral standing pause and preserve visible physical continuity into the canopy.
Must Preserve: Visible orientation away from interaction; no neutral standing pause; direct transition from feeding/rest into locomotion; committed movement toward canopy; physically resolved contact with branch or trunk; continuous post-contact motion rather than pose reset; concise exit that clearly removes the Topic Gibbon from the interaction area
Can Vary: Starting posture; pivot direction; route A vs route B; number of acceleration steps or climbing beats; lead foot/hand; launch angle; branch/trunk height; first post-contact action; whether final state is swing, pull-up, perch or disappearance behind canopy
Avoid: Fading/teleporting away; full stand-and-pause before leaving; arms dropping to neutral between feeding and movement; hard cut from ground to canopy; stopping under a branch before jumping; static pose immediately after catch; climbing with passive feet; overly long exit that competes with the completed user task
V1 Simplification: Default V1 exit: orient away → forward shift + rise → 2–3 brisk strides → upward-forward leap + overhead reach → catch → one short pendulum/pull-up → disappear into canopy. Optional alternate when a trunk is nearby: pivot away → short ground launch → trunk catch → 2–3 hand/foot-assisted climbing beats → perch/disappear. Reuse established gait, catch and ascent mechanics.
Open Questions: Closed for V1. Two independent end-to-end departure sequences now cover different exit geometries and starting transitions.
